correctness.rationale: On the exact real Banaś--Frączek unit ball B={u²+v²≤1, |u|≤1/λ}, the Euclidean/strip active-branch split is exhaustive. The same-Euclidean branch is bounded by 2√(1+τ²), the same-strip branch by 2, and the mixed branch by support functions. The identity (λ²−1)(λ−t)²−(1−t²)=λ²−2+(−λ²+λt+1)²≥0 for λ≥√2 guarantees the two shifted directions expose the cut circular vertices. Maximizing their sum gives G(τ)=(1+τ+√(1+2κτ+τ²))/2 for κ=1−2/λ²; x=(1/λ,√(1−1/λ²)), y=(−1/λ,√(1−1/λ²)) attains equality for all 0≤τ≤1, with correctly identified active branches. The Baronti--Papini unit-sphere reduction converts this to 2^(1/p)G(τ)/(1+τ^p)^(1/p). Explicit p=2 logarithmic differentiation is nonnegative, and τ^(p−1)/(1+τ^p)≤τ/(1+τ²) for p≥2 transfers the result; G itself increases for p=∞. Thus the maximum at τ=1 equals 1+√(1−λ^(−2)), including λ=√2 and both p endpoints. These are analytic uniform proofs, not finite data.
